Subject: Catalyst Health — production degradation after r7-quant upgrade

Hi Jonas / Laura,

We started seeing a sharp increase in request latency and a rise in 5xx errors across our inference endpoints after you rolled r7-quant into production last night (~00:45 PDT). P99 latency is spiking from ~220ms to ~1.8s and overall throughput has dropped ~30%. We're also seeing a handful of bad outputs where the model hallucinates medication names in clinical summaries (attached sample).

This is blocking several downstream jobs and our frontline clinicians are reporting delays. Can you confirm whether the change you shipped included a quantization profile change? We need an immediate mitigation plan — rollback or hotfix.

I've attached our latency dashboard snapshot and a sample of the failed responses. Please advise next steps and estimated ETA to recovery.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director of Product Operations
Catalyst Health

Subject: Re: Catalyst Health — production degradation after r7-quant upgrade

Folks — preliminary SRE triage below. TL;DR: regression correlates with r7-quant rollout at 00:45 PDT. The quant profile (q4_8_bfloat) introduced a larger per-token decode loop and increased CPU fallback on some machines, which explains both latency and throughput drop. We're also seeing an uptick in transient model OOMs on smaller hosts, which returns 5xx for those requests.

What I've collected so far:
- Timeline: r7-quant promoted 00:45 PDT; errors spike at 00:50–01:20 PDT.
- P99 increased: 220ms -> 1.8s.
- 5xx rate: baseline 0.3% -> 1.9% (mainly on summarization route).
- Root cause hypothesis: the q4_8_bfloat kernel path has a regression in KV-cache eviction under continuous batching that thrashes some hosts.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Pinning impacted routing to r7-fp16 for latency-sensitive routes (will reduce quality delta).
- Draining and reprovisioning 4 affected small hosts (estimated 25 min).
- If pin fails, plan B is a quick rollback of the r7-quant deploy (requires approval).

I've uploaded debug logs and a regression tradeoff report to the incident doc. See attachments for quick artifacts.

3) Post-mortem: we'll deliver a triage note, root cause, and recommended guardrails for future quant profile rollouts.

We will keep your leadership updated every hour. Jonas will coordinate the cadence; Ava will own the MAP and rollback comms.

Subject: Re: Catalyst Health — production degradation after r7-quant upgrade

Update for Catalyst leadership — short summary and next steps:

1) What happened: a quantization profile (q4_8_bfloat) in the r7-quant model triggered a kernel path that increased per-request CPU fallback and caused KV-cache eviction instability under continuous batching. This produced higher p99 latency and a rise in transient 5xx on smaller hosts.
2) Actions taken: Dylan's team pinned critical summarization traffic to r7-fp16 and reprovisioned the affected hosts. We measured improvement: p99 is down from 1.8s -> ~360ms and 5xx rate has fallen to 0.5%.
3) Next steps:
   - We'll perform a tenant-wide rollback of r7-quant tomorrow at 02:00 PDT if internal validation of the pin + reprovisioning does not hold during a 12-hour monitoring window.
   - We'll share a detailed postmortem and a mitigation plan (deployment gating for quant profiles + synthetic regression tests) by EOD Monday.

Attachments included: latency_dashboard_jul09.png, regression_tradeoff_report_v2.pdf, sre_debug_log_2026-07-09.txt

Jonas Weber
